findings.title: Charismatic must place the available warrior before entering Turmoil

summary_evidence.exact: **Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** Each card requires:
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

source_refs: publisher-faq-source-metadata.json lines 2–9: Leder Games Root English live printing p16; retrieved 2026-11-05T14:09:21.112Z; individual FAQ publication date not displayed
findings.source_requirement: The supplied official FAQ expressly answers the Charismatic one-warrior supply case by requiring the one available warrior to be placed. Combining this with the Law full-action Turmoil rule means perform that maximum possible placement, then enter Turmoil because the two-warrior requirement was not fulfilled.
findings.why_material: The repeated unconditional instruction to immediately enter Turmoil on incomplete actions, specifically including warrior supply, can make a player leave the last warrior in supply. That changes the map state. The correct general maximum-placement statement at line 109 does not specify which instruction acts first, and the Eyrie section gives no partial-placement-before-Turmoil exception/clarification. This is an operational ambiguity/important omission, not a claim that the summary explicitly says zero warriors.
findings.expected_interaction: With Charismatic, a legal matching roost and only one warrior in supply: place that warrior at the chosen roost, then enter Turmoil; do not continue the Decree.
findings.recommended_clarification: State the maximum-possible placement occurs before Turmoil when a Decree placement cannot be fulfilled, with the Charismatic one-warrior example. This is audit feedback only; summary was not edited.
findings.reasoning_status: Sequencing is an inference combining the supplied explicit publisher answer with Law 7.5.2/7.7; no FAQ publication date or historical edition equivalence inferred.
